data.title: People’s Party takes flak over handling of abuse
data.description: Activists working to combat gender-based violence have called on the People's Party (PP) to apologise to former MP Tisana Choonhavan over its handling of her sexual abuse allegations and launch an independent investigation into the case.

data.title: Firms welcome govt bid to scrap red tape
data.description: The private sector has welcomed the government's accelerating efforts to remove laws and regulations that hamper business, saying the initiative would sharpen the country's competitiveness.

data.title: Missing German man found dead
data.description: PHUKET: The body of a 30-year-old German tourist who went missing after being swept out to sea at Freedom Beach has been found.

data.title: Lion café probed over bitten tourist
data.description: PHUKET: The Tourist Assistance Centre (TAC) has inspected a lion café following social media reports that a Chinese tourist was bitten by a lion.

data.title: Govt orders password reset after data leak
data.description: The government has ordered more than 300 departments to reset passwords immediately and inspect 30,000 systems to prevent further state data leaks.

data.title: PM wants default child safety settings
data.description: <p>Thailand will push for child protection settings to be enabled by default on new digital devices, aiming to shield young users from harmful online content without any parental setup required.</p>

data.title: PP takes flak over handling of abuse
data.description: A coalition of 16 organisations working to combat gender-based violence has called on the People's Party (PP) to apologise to former MP Tisana Choonhavan over its handling of her sexual abuse allegations and launch an independent investigation into the case.

data.title: Flood risks push up rail budget: SRT
data.description: <p>The State Railway of Thailand (SRT) has raised the budget for its southern double-track railway projects to 122.72 billion baht after flood risks and construction costs increased.</p>

data.title: BMA steps up checks on city nightspots
data.description: Bangkok is intensifying inspections of entertainment venues after checks found shortcomings involving fire safety, escape routes and building materials.

data.title: Exam process 'riddled with risks'
data.description: A committee has uncovered vulnerabilities that facilitated fraud at almost every stage of last year's local government civil service examination, it says.

data.title: NBTC freezes up over controversy
data.description: A dispute over the National Broadcasting and Telecommunications Commission (NBTC) chairman Dr Sarana Boonbaichaiyapruck's eligibility has escalated, with Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul signing a submission seeking a Royal Command for his removal.

data.title: More heavy rain threatens already flooded provinces
data.description: Flooding has worsened in Nakhon Phanom and Bueng Kan as swollen rivers inundate farmland, while heavy rain has triggered flash floods in Lampang.

data.title: Fixed-term licences eyed
data.description: The government is considering introducing fixed-term firearms possession licences as part of a comprehensive overhaul of Thailand's 1947 firearms law.

data.title: Military ties 'not linked' to trade talks with US
data.description: <p>The government has no plans to use military and security cooperation with the United States as a bargaining chip in trade negotiations, a spokeswoman says.</p>

data.title: First half 2026 sees some 1 million new cases, mostly drug related, reaching first instance courts
data.description: The Court of First Instance received 1.11 million cases in the first half of 2026 with most filed in Pathum Thani province and most criminal cases concerning narcotics.

data.title: Govt clarifies self-defence stance on gun controls
data.description: The government sought to allay concerns Wednesday that proposed gun-control measures would undermine the public's right to self-defence, stating that no decision has been made to impose a blanket ban on firearms and that public feedback is being considered.

data.title: Classes suspended by shooting rampage to resume online from Aug 18
data.description: Debsirin Nonthaburi School classes that were suspended following a fatal shooting rampage on Aug 7 have been ordered to resume from Aug 18 but are to remain online until the end of the month.

data.title: Missing forest rangers on illegal mining patrol found safe
data.description: KANCHANABURI - Three forest rangers from Thong Pha Phum National Park who went missing while patrolling for illegal gold mining were found safe in the Pilok mountains on Wednesday.

data.title: 24 illegal workers arrested at Chinese data centre project in Rayong
data.description: RAYONG - A raid on illegal migrant workers netted 24 Myanmar and Chinese nationals at the construction site of a Chinese-run data centre on Tuesday.

data.title: UNCLOS conciliation chair to be named this week
data.description: <p>A chairperson for the compulsory conciliation process under the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) will be selected on Friday, with the first meeting of the conciliation commission expected next month, Foreign Affairs Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said.</p>

data.title: Ukrainian scam suspect arrested in Phuket
data.description: PHUKET: Immigration police in the nation's popular southern island province arrested a 26-year-old Ukrainian man wanted under an Interpol Red Notice for alleged investment scams on Tuesday.

data.title: PP MP cranks up pressure on NACC
data.description: People's Party (PP) list-MP and opposition chief whip Parit Wacharasindhu has stepped up pressure on the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) to investigate politicians allegedly linked to the manipulation of the 2024 Senate election.

data.title: CSD submits exam fraud files to NACC
data.description: Crime Suppression Division (CSD) investigators have submitted more than 3,000 pages of documents in the civil service exam fraud case to the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) for consideration in legal action.

data.title: Court sets Nov 23 for Facebook lawsuits
data.description: A legal battle brought by the Thailand Consumers Council against businesses allegedly involved in online scams conducted through Facebook has moved forward, with the Bangkok South Civil Court scheduling the next hearing for Nov 23.
